title: Pekudei: as the Lord commanded
hookLine: the phrase repeats as each piece is finished

cards: Read Exodus straight through and something about the last chapters can feel strange.
From chapter twenty-five to thirty-one, God describes the sanctuary in detail: the ark, the table, the lampstand, the curtains, the priest's clothes.
Then, from chapter thirty-five to the end, the Torah describes it all again, piece by piece, as it gets made. Same ark. Same lampstand.
A book that rarely wastes a word repeats itself for chapters. And in the final stretch, one short phrase keeps coming back, like the chorus of a song.

teach.b: The phrase, in the JPS 1917 translation, is "as the LORD commanded Moses." They made the priest's garments, as the LORD commanded Moses. They made the breastplate, as the LORD commanded Moses.
The gold plate, the robe, the tunics, and then, as Moses sets up the tent, every piece he puts in place, the same words. Tradition counts eighteen of them in the closing chapters.
One teaching, recorded in the Jerusalem Talmud, connects that number to the eighteen blessings of the Amidah, the standing prayer at the heart of Jewish worship. Why describe the sanctuary twice?
Commentators have offered many answers, and one of the simplest is that the second telling is the plans coming true. Not a repeat: a promise kept, item by item. Think back a few chapters.
The golden calf was also something the people made with their gold and their skill. But God never asked for it. It came from fear and impatience, and from what they wanted in the moment.

teach.h: NOT THE CALF: WHAT WAS ASKED.
teach.b: Here, the same people, with the same gifts and the same hands, make exactly what was asked, nothing more and nothing less.
Rashi, at the opening of this portion, calls the finished sanctuary a testimony that the calf had been forgiven. It's also a very ordinary virtue: doing a thing the way you said you would.
The Torah slows down to honor it, eighteen times.

how: Vayakhel and Pekudei, which retell the building of the sanctuary, are often read together on one Shabbat in non-leap years, closing the reading of Exodus.

practice: Think of something you've told someone you'd do, call by Friday, fix the shelf, be there at seven, and choose one. Picture doing it exactly as you said, nothing skipped, nothing added, and handing it over finished.

wordCard.voice: Pekudei. The portion where each finished piece of the sanctuary ends with the same words: as the Lord commanded Moses.

orig.note: Hebrew: as the Lord commanded Moses. The divine name is read aloud as Adonai.
